verdict.rationale: Aider documents checks well: it lints edited files by default, runs tests via /test or automatically with --test-cmd/--auto-test, and runs code with /run. Diff inspection is only indirect: Aider auto-commits each edit so changes can be reviewed in git history or through raw /git commands, with no dedicated diff-review view and nothing tied to a merge gate. missing for 10: a documented first-party diff-inspection command or view, an explicit pre-merge review workflow, and independent hands-on corroboration of the lint/test checks.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect diffs and run checks to catch problems before merging

citations.quote: Whenever aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message. This makes it easy to undo or review aider’s changes.
Go back in the git history to review the changes that aider made to your code
By default, aider will lint any files which it edits.
You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
